activity.notes: Nur ad-Din's rule begins with his accession in Aleppo after Imad ad-Din Zengi's death in 1146 and ends with his death in 1174. The polity is stored as the Zengid dynastic state rather than modern Syria; no anachronistic modern-state identity is created.

sources.title: NÛREDDİN ZENGÎ, Mahmud — TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.citation_text: TDV identifies Nur al-Din Mahmud Zengi as atabeg of Damascus and Aleppo from 1146 to 1174 and describes his accession at Aleppo after his father's death.

sources.title: Nūr al-Dīn and Saladin, 1146–1193 — The Cambridge History of the Crusades
sources.citation_text: Cambridge treats Nur al-Din's accession in 1146 as the start of the documented political period preceding Saladin and situates him within the Zangid dynasty.
